svg.text: D-E SPIT AND STATIONS — hold the food, not the tool
A kitchen lathe: the food is held between a spindle and a tail rod and presented to simple tools on one sliding, swinging tool rod.
spindle 0–600 rpm, 10 Nm · tail rod push 20–150 N
tool rod: slide 320, swing ±60°, 125 N at 120 mm
10 axes · 4 circular seals at the lathe
END VIEW along the spindle: the swing selects the tool
six tools on arms: peeler, knife, comb, brush, grater, gouge
swing motor current = the tool force sensor

g.text: filled slice from the press table
1/6 The turret hand sets a potato on the spindle fork; the tail rod pushes its cup against the other end.
2/6 Spindle turns at 120 rpm; the sprung peeler slides 12 mm per turn along the potato. Peel → waste.
3/6 The tool rod swings to the comb: it scores meridians to the core while the spindle indexes.
4/6 Diverter to the pot; the parting knife slices at the dice pitch — each slice falls apart into dice.
5/6 Egg between two vacuum cups: a scribe scores the equator, the tail rod pulls back, the contents drop whole.
6/6 Rouladen: a slotted mandrel takes the edge of the filled slice and winds it 2.5 turns into a tight roll.
